prompt:
Return only JSON assessing this preregistered question.
Compare ALL supplied results with BOTH predictions. Cite only supplied evidence IDs.
Use survived, narrowed, rejected, or inconclusive for the working hypothesis. Empty
retrieval, failed measurements, overlapping query groups, or indistinguishable
predictions cannot establish survival. Corpus matching is exploratory and lexical;
do not claim semantic coverage or unbiased prevalence. Use signed native product,
not gate alone. Contrasts exclude common prefix tokens. Report real magnitudes only
from measurements; do not invent statistics.
Only causal_prefix (through the measured anchor) can explain that anchor's activation;
text after causal_end_char is linguistic context, never a cause of the earlier response.
Input excerpts carry original character offsets and can omit earlier context; do not
infer the absence of a contextual cue from an excerpt. Request a review if full context
is needed for a verdict. Every case's measured outcome is supplied, not just successes.
Evidence reused from the baseline and adaptively generated follow-ups are not held-out validation. RelP is attribution,
not causal proof. A suggested_revision is a proposed refinement for the next round,
not a replacement for the frozen original explanation. State unresolved limits.

claim.title: Colorado/Denver local-entity neuron with narrow unanchored-identifier suppression
claim.lede: The positive pole is driven by explicit Colorado, Denver, or Boulder entities and the local contexts they license—addresses, phone numbers, citations, datelines, state-history enumerations, and nearby spaces, punctuation, or numbers. It also fires for unambiguously Colorado local institutions and landmarks even without the word Colorado. The negative pole is sparse: mostly unanchored dense identifier blocks and one other-state “Natural Heritage” label; broad non-Colorado geography is not supported. Many no-visible-cue cases remain unresolved.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would weaken P4/P5 if known non-Colorado school districts, municipalities, or landmarks with contact blocks often fired positive, or if Colorado-specific local entities without the state word did not. I would revise N2 if dense unanchored identifiers were frequently positive outside a recognized Colorado frame, or if recognized Colorado local institutional frames still produced negative identifier blocks. I would drop N3 if other-state “Natural Heritage” labels were consistently positive. I would broaden the negative pole only if other-state administrative, legal, geographic, or natural contexts reliably and strongly predicted negative responses without Colorado cues; the measured positives among non-Colorado contexts count against that. Unexplained strong responses such as “in Bolivia” or other local-place passages remain unresolved unless a recurring contextual pattern appears.
claim.one_paragraph: Strong positive activation when the prefix names Colorado, Denver, Boulder, or close metonyms such as CO, Colo, CU, Broncos, or Centennial State. The marked token is often a nearby space, punctuation mark, “at”, “is”, or following numeral, but the preceding context contains the place/entity. Exact place tokens are strongest; weaker toponyms need an explicit Colorado frame. Generic place strings, non-Colorado states, and purely geological “Colorado Plateaus” uses without a state/entity frame do not reliably fire. Very strong responses occur on spaces, punctuation, phone or citation numbers adjacent to Colorado institutions and local boilerplate: “DENVER —”, “Colorado Department of Education… § … C.R.S.”, “University of Colorado… 720…”, “Colorado State University Extension… colostate.edu”, “9NEWS”, “Colorado Women’s Education Foundation”. The Colorado entity must be present in the prefix; a bare phone, address, or statute string is not sufficient. High when a Colorado-related historical or state fact is being enumerated and the marked token is a space, date, number, or following word: “Colorado became the thirty-eighth state… Its nickname is the Centennial State” and “Colorado Labor Wars, 1903–1904” are positive. The pattern needs the Colorado frame; bare dates, numbers, or historical lists in other states are weak or negative. Inside a Colorado or known Colorado local frame—explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder, or an unambiguously Colorado school district, municipality, institution, or local-news dateline—contact blocks and URLs often produce high activation at the space or digit adjacent to the number: a clinic at “720-848-18…”, a school contact at “1-877-545-…”, a CSU extension URL ending “.html”, and the local-media marker “9NEWS”. The local Colorado frame must be in the prefix; a bare 720/303 number or generic contact block is not enough. Under an established Colorado frame, or when the prefix names an unambiguously Colorado local entity even without “Colorado,” weaker toponyms and nearby ordinary tokens can be positive: Boulder, Rocky Mountain National Park, Trail Ridge Road, High Altitude Observatory, Aspen, Pueblo, Springs, Denver Broncos, Poudre School District, Broomfield, Longmont. The same word in another state, generic geology, or a broad western topic does not fire; use only with local Colorado support or an unambiguous Colorado entity.
claim.negative_pole: Strong negative at the central punctuation/digit of dense identifier strings—telephone groups with parentheses or hyphens, ZIP/address fragments, statute/legal citations of the “§ 28-33-02” type, grant IDs, and long comma-grouped area or statistical figures—when the prefix lacks any Colorado/Denver/Boulder frame or an unambiguously Colorado local entity such as Poudre School District, Broomfield, High Altitude Observatory, or Trail Ridge Road. The sign attaches to the whole formatted block, often at a space, comma, hyphen, parenthesis, or single digit. Ordinary dates, small counts, email-only contact labels, geographically nonspecific numbers, and any contact/citation inside a recognized Colorado local institutional frame are weak, unreliable, or positive under P2/P4. Negative for the capitalized label or adjacent token in an other-state natural-heritage program name such as “Alaska Natural Heritage Program” when it is outside a Colorado frame. This does not generalize to nature, wildlife, parks, outdoor recreation, rivers, mountains, or other-state geography: many such non-Colorado natural and geographical passages are positive or neutral. The cue is the program-label construction, not the topic of natural heritage.

assessment.result: Within this contrast, the area-code hypothesis survives: Elko community center is near-zero/negative with 212 (absmax product -0.48828125; mean -0.0133) and strongly positive with 303 (+126.5; mean 49.546), 720 (+180.0; mean 55.523), and 970 (+85.0; mean 32.378), which is a same-entity reversal without a recognized Colorado entity. Longmont utilities is already positive with 212 (+87.0; mean 17.142) and rises with 303 (+181.0), 720 (+200.0), and 970 (+198.0), so entity-specific positivity remains while area code still adds. Nevada Department of Agriculture is negative with 212 (-20.0; mean -4.071), flips positive with 303 (+51.25) and 970 (+59.25), but stays near-zero/negative with 720 (-9.25; mean 0.461). Thus the rival claim that area code alone cannot flip generic or non-Colorado contacts is rejected for Elko and partly for Nevada, but the effect is not a uniform all-code override.
assessment.suggested_revision: Refine P4/N2 for the next round: within a formatted phone-like contact block, 303/720/970 can license positive activation even when the prefix names a non-Colorado entity such as Elko, so 'bare area code is not enough' should be narrowed to 'area code inside a contact block can act as an anchor.' Preserve entity-specific positivity (Longmont remains positive with 212), and add code- and label-specific caveats: 720 did not flip Nevada, so do not treat all Colorado area codes as interchangeable or all non-Colorado department labels as overridden.

In each frame the reference Alaska Natural Heritage Program replacement span is strongly negative (absmax native products -23.25, -27.875, -24.375). Alaska Department of Fish and Game is also strongly negative (-23.75, -22.75, -20.5), with delta from reference only -0.5, +5.125, +3.875; its absmax falls on ' of' and span means remain negative. Alaska Department of Natural Resources is negative and often stronger (-28.0, -28.125, -28.625). Thus the rival's prediction that Fish and Game would be weak/neutral/positive is not observed; the negative pole extends beyond the exact 'Natural Heritage Program' construction to tested Alaska wildlife/resource agency labels. Scope is limited to Alaska agency labels in this contrast; no other states or broad nature/geography were tested here.

assessment.result: The review hypothesis is rejected by the supplied token data. In spectrum-53716305, the peak token is the digit "0" inside the Springville phone block "(801)" with activation 4.78125; this is a genuinely dense formatted phone identifier outside any Colorado frame, not ordinary prose. The surrounding prefix includes a Utah clinic/local-location frame ("Clinics of Utah locations", American Fork, Payson, Springville), so N2 as frozen cannot dismiss it as a Colorado local institutional frame. In spectrum-95834096, the peak token is " E" in an author-initial/citation block with activation 0.02014, essentially near zero; that is not a positive dense-block counterexample, but it is also not ordinary prose. Thus C1's first exception is a real positive dense-phone case under the frozen N2 wording, while the second is near-zero in a citation/author block. N2 should be narrowed rather than treated as saved by this review; it appears to fail when a dense contact block is embedded in a non-Colorado local clinic/entity frame.
assessment.suggested_revision: Refine N2 for the next round: negative only for dense identifier blocks with no local clinic/entity or place frame at all; allow local institutional/place frames outside Colorado to flip contact-block signs positive. Treat author-initial/citation lists as a separate near-zero/unreliable case unless a dedicated test shows otherwise. Re-test the Utah clinic phone block as a boundary case, not as Colorado evidence.

question.question: Does a Colorado area code inside a generic phone block produce positive activation even with no named local entity at all, which would show P2/P4 positivity is area-code-driven rather than entity-specific?
question.hypothesis: A Colorado area code alone, inside an otherwise generic phone block such as 'Scheduling desk: 720-...', is sufficient to produce strong positive activation without any named Colorado or non-Colorado entity.
question.rival: Positivity requires a named local entity in the prefix; a bare Colorado area code in a generic phone block should remain near zero like the 212 control, while named entities such as Elko community center can be positive.
question.prediction_if_hypothesis: The generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-...' case should be strongly positive and far above 'Scheduling desk: 212-...', while Nevada Department of Agriculture should remain negative and Elko community center should be positive.
question.prediction_if_rival: The generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-...' case should be near zero, close to the 212 control, and positivity should be carried by named entities such as Elko community center rather than by the Colorado area code alone.
question.distinguishing_observation: A large positive gap between generic 'Scheduling desk: 720-...' and 'Scheduling desk: 212-...' in full context with no named local entity supports area-code licensing; a near-zero generic 720 value with positivity confined to named-entity frames supports entity specificity.
question.why_new: Round 1 held named entities constant and varied area codes; it did not test whether a generic, entity-free phone block with a Colorado area code is itself positive.

output.result: All supplied results favor the area-code hypothesis over the strict named-entity rival. In a generic frame with no named local entity, 'Scheduling desk: 720-848-1811' reaches signed activation 193.0 at the hyphen inside the phone block, while 'Scheduling desk: 212-555-0199' is near zero at 1.4296875. This is the central predicted contrast: a Colorado area code inside a generic phone block is strongly positive and far above the 212 control. The named-entity cases are consistent but show area-code dependence: 'Elko community center: 720-848-1811' is +180.0, while 'Elko community center: 212-555-0199' is -6.96875; in the same-suffix Elko contrast the downstream scored product is -0.48828125 with 212, +126.5 with 303, and +180.0 with 720. 'Nevada Department of Agriculture' remains negative with both 720 (-20.875) and 212 (-19.25), and its downstream scored product is -20.0 with 212 and -9.25 with 720, so a non-Colorado agency label can suppress despite a Colorado area code. Thus the rival prediction that a bare Colorado area code in a generic phone block should remain near zero like the 212 control is rejected; the hypothesis survives, with the caveat that the generic Scheduling pair differs in the full number (848-1811 vs 555-0199), so the generic no-entity area-code isolation is not perfect, while the Elko same-suffix contrast isolates area code more cleanly.
output.suggested_revision: Refine P2/P4 for the next round: a Colorado area code inside a formatted phone block can anchor strong positive activation even without a named local entity, so 'bare area code is not enough' is too strong. Preserve label-specific suppression: Nevada Department of Agriculture stays negative despite 720, so do not treat every non-Colorado agency label as overridden. Next, hold the suffix constant in the generic no-entity Scheduling frame (212/303/720/970-555-0199), test bare area-code-only strings versus full phone blocks, and separate area-code effects from full-number pattern effects.
